Add AG2 connector tools to the existing local repo C:/Users/mariu/ventures/freight-recovery-ag2 (local git; commits c5ff981 pipelines, ee3a7c3 secrets; 70 tests passing; files pipelines/{common,value_research,build_mirror,claim_pipeline}.py, [SENSITIVE_PATH] (gitignored values, README), docs/secrets.md, [SENSITIVE_PATH]). Read those first and follow their conventions (key loading order env → *_FILE → [SENSITIVE_PATH]<name>; never print or log secret values). Commit locally with the Co-Authored-By trailer; never push. Do not touch any other repo.

User decisions: services = ALL THREE below; operations = READ + CREATE (no update, no delete).

Follow the ag2-tool-builder connector pattern: autogen `@tool()` functions returning JSON strings; shared `_get_headers()` / `_make_request()` per connector using httpx with 30s timeout; error mapping 401→"connector_setup_required:<id>", 403 permission denied, 404 not found, 429 rate limit; limit/offset with capped limit; input validation before any call. Read the skill file for the exact pattern: C:/Users/mariu/.[REDACTED:high_entropy].md (check the installed autogen version's real `tool` import/decorator signature in the repo's venv and use what actually exists).

Put them in connectors/{common.py,freight_recovery.py,data_source.py,github.py} + tests/.

1. Freight Recovery API (our own platform). Read the real API-key-authenticated routes, scopes, header format and rate limits from C:/Users/mariu/ventures/freight-recovery-build (branch feat/intelligence; READ ONLY — other agents are working there): api/src (route registration + API key scope checks), and the step-4 spec at C:/Users/mariu/.[REDACTED:high_entropy].md (A12 API keys, PUBLIC CONTRACT). Only wrap routes that API keys can actually reach; read tools for everything readable, create tools only where the API exposes a create to API keys (if none, say so and ship read-only — do NOT invent endpoints). Base URL from FREIGHT_RECOVERY_BASE_URL (must be https unless host is localhost/127.0.0.1); key FREIGHT_RECOVERY_API_KEY via the secrets loader ([SENSITIVE_PATH]freight_recovery_api_key). Key goes ONLY in the Authorization: Bearer header, never in URLs/params/logs.
2. Data source: read the untracked list C:/Users/mariu/ventures/freight-recovery/docs/data-sources.md (read only). Pick the ONE source most useful for freight-claim recovery that has a documented public HTTP API with clear terms (cite the doc URL and terms you relied on; fetch docs with WebFetch only if your tools allow, otherwise use what's in the file and mark unverified). Read tools only unless that API genuinely has a sensible create; explain the choice in the README. If no source qualifies, stop and report why instead of guessing.
3. GitHub: read tools (list/get PRs, workflow runs + failed-job log summary, issues) and create tools limited to: create issue, create issue/PR comment. Token GITHUB_TOKEN via the secrets loader (document least-privilege fine-grained PAT scopes). Repo allowlist from FR_GITHUB_REPOS (comma list, default empty → tools refuse) so agents cannot write to arbitrary repos.

Safety for ALL create tools: parameter `confirm: bool = False`; when False return {"success": true, "dry_run": true, "would_send": <method, path, redacted payload>} and make no request. Idempotency-Key header where the API supports it. Plus: path segments validated (regex) and URL-quoted (no path traversal / host override); fixed base URL per connector (no caller-supplied URLs → no SSRF); response bodies truncated (e.g. 20 KB) and never echo auth headers; honour Retry-After on 429 with at most 2 bounded retries for GET only (never auto-retry POST); error text scrubbed of anything matching the token value.

Tests (pytest, no real network: use httpx.MockTransport or respx if already installed — do not add new deps without noting them; prefer MockTransport): auth missing → connector_setup_required; 401/403/404/429 mapping; limit cap; dry-run default makes zero requests; confirm=True sends exactly one POST with Idempotency-Key; path traversal rejected; repo allowlist enforced; token never appears in any returned string or log record (caplog); https enforcement. Update README, docs/secrets.md (new secrets: FREIGHT_RECOVERY_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, any data-source key) and [SENSITIVE_PATH] (names only, no values). Run the full test suite.

handback.t:
I added the AG2 connector tools for all three services in C:/Users/mariu/ventures/freight-recovery-ag2 and committed them locally as 6ff2e25 (with the Co-Authored-By trailer). Nothing was pushed and no other repo was written to. The full suite passes: 174 passed, 1 skipped (the existing 70 plus 104 new tests). No new packages were added: httpx 0.28.1 was already in the lock through ag2/anthropic; I pinned it directly and the hash lock only changed one `# via` line.

This was a side task with no run directory, so there is no implementation.md or mailbox entry.

**Files** (all under C:/Users/mariu/ventures/freight-recovery-ag2)
- New: connectors/__init__.py (has `all_tools()`), connectors/common.py, connectors/freight_recovery.py, connectors/data_source.py, connectors/github.py
- New tests: tests/connector_helpers.py, tests/test_connectors_common.py, tests/test_connector_freight_recovery.py, tests/test_connector_data_source.py, tests/test_connector_github.py
- Changed: tests/conftest.py (new autouse fixture: clears connector env vars, hides the default secret files, fails any request that isn't mocked, makes Retry-After waits instant), README.md (new "Connector tools" section), docs/secrets.md (3 new inventory rows, least-privilege scopes, handover steps, wider history-scan regex), [SENSITIVE_PATH]README.md (the new secret files plus create/rotate/revoke steps), [SENSITIVE_PATH] (names only), requirements.in and requirements.txt.

**Decorator check:** ag2 0.14.0 has `from autogen.tools import tool`, with signature `tool(name=None, description=None)`, and it returns a `Tool`. The `Tool` checks argument types with pydantic before my code runs, so a non-integer passed as `number` is rejected before any request; one test covers this.

**1. Freight Recovery API** (key only in `Authorization: Bearer`; base URL from FREIGHT_RECOVERY_BASE_URL plus `/api/v1`)

API keys can reach exactly 9 routes: those whose access declares an `apiKeyScope`, checked in api-key-auth.ts:153-155. Scopes are defined at packages/shared/src/api-key-dto.ts:11-18 and match spec Q13. I wrapped all 9; source lines are in freight-recovery-build/api/src:

| Tool | Route | Scope | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fr_list_claims` (read) | GET /claims | claims.read | claims/routes.ts:29-35 |
| `fr_get_claim` (read) | GET /claims/:id | claims.read | claims/routes.ts:37-43 |
| `fr_list_claim_documents` (read) | GET /claims/:id/documents | claims.read | imports/routes.ts:193-199 |
| `fr_export_claims_csv` (read) | GET /exports/claims | exports.claims | exports/routes.ts:119-137 |
| `fr_list_import_batches` (read) | GET /imports | imports.write | imports/routes.ts:79-85 |
| `fr_get_import_batch` (read) | GET /imports/:batchId | imports.write | imports/routes.ts:87-97 |
| `fr_get_import_document` (read) | GET /imports/:batchId/documents/:docId | imports.write | imports/routes.ts:99-109 |
| `fr_create_import_batch` (create) | POST /imports | imports.write | imports/routes.ts:67-77 |
| `fr_upload_import_document` (create) | POST /imports/:batchId/documents?filename= | imports.write | imports/routes.ts:210-217 |

- The upload tool takes the file as base64 (capped at 10 MiB, the server default), never a file path.
- Header format: http/security.ts:66-72. The server's guard against `fr_live_` appearing in URLs is at security.ts:94.
- Rate limits: per key `RATE_LIMIT_API_KEY_MAX` = 300 per 60 s, and failed attempts `RATE_LIMIT_API_KEY_FAIL_MAX` = 30 per 600 s per IP (app.ts:225-229; config.ts:244-245). The 429 response carries Retry-After (app.ts:77).
- Every other route answers an API key with 403, so I wrapped nothing else.

**2. Data source: FMCSA QCMobile** (data_source.py, read-only; the API has no writes)

| Tool | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| `fmcsa_get_carrier` | /carriers/{dot} |
| `fmcsa_search_carriers_by_name` | /carriers/name/{name}, paged with start/size |
| `fmcsa_get_carrier_by_docket` | /carriers/docket-number/{n}; strips an MC/MX/FF prefix |
| `fmcsa_get_carrier_authority` | /carriers/{dot}/authority |
| `fmcsa_get_carrier_cargo_carried` | /carriers/{dot}/cargo-carried |
| `fmcsa_get_carrier_oos` | /carriers/{dot}/oos |
| `fmcsa_get_carrier_docket_numbers` | /carriers/{dot}/docket-numbers |

- **Why this one:** data-sources.md section 11 lists it as a free official API, and it is in the "Recommended free, official starting set". A claim has to name the liable legal entity, and the USDOT/MC number on the bill of lading or rate confirmation resolves to legal name, address, authority and out-of-service status. The other freight sources in the file are paid partner APIs.
- **Key handling:** FMCSA_WEBKEY (default file [SENSITIVE_PATH]fmcsa_webkey). QCMobile requires the key as a `?webKey=` query parameter, which goes against the "never in URLs" rule you set for our own key. Results only ever show the path without the query, and httpx's log line containing the URL is scrubbed to `webKey=[REDACTED]` (tested).

**3. GitHub** (`https://api.github.com`, token GITHUB_TOKEN, default file [SENSITIVE_PATH]github_token)
- Read: `gh_list_pull_requests`, `gh_get_pull_request`, `gh_list_workflow_runs`, `gh_get_failed_jobs_summary` (failed steps, `##[error]` lines and log tail for up to 3 jobs), `gh_list_issues`, `gh_get_issue`.
- Create: `gh_create_issue`, `gh_create_comment` (works on issues and PRs).
- The FR_GITHUB_REPOS allowlist applies to every tool, reads included. Empty means every tool refuses; an invalid entry reports `connector_setup_required:github`.
- Job logs are fetched by following GitHub's 302 by hand, without the token, and only to `*.actions.githubusercontent.com` or `*.blob.core.windows.net`.
- GitHub's 403 rate-limit responses (`x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, or a Retry-After header) are mapped to the rate-limit error.
- The documented fine-grained token permissions are: Metadata Read, Pull requests Read, Actions Read, Issues Read and write.

**Safety measures** (in common.py)
- Create tools default to `confirm=False`, which returns the dry-run result and makes no request. `confirm=True` sends exactly one POST with an Idempotency-Key (generated, or supplied by the caller), and POSTs are never retried.
- Payloads containing a secret or anything shaped like one are refused.
- Path segments are checked with a regex and URL-quoted, and the final URL must stay on the base origin and path. Callers can never supply a URL.
- GETs retry at most twice on 429, and only when Retry-After is 10 s or less.
- Responses are cut to 20 KB; GitHub responses are first reduced to the useful fields.
- Every returned string and every log record from httpx, httpcore and connectors is scrubbed of loaded secret values and credential-shaped strings.
- httpx runs with `trust_env=False` and `follow_redirects=False`.
- I confirmed the leak tests have teeth: with scrubbing switched off, 4 of them fail.

**Tests:** 104 new, all using httpx.MockTransport (respx is not installed). They cover:
- missing key or URL returning `connector_setup_required`
- the 401/403/404/429/500 mapping, plus GitHub's 403 rate-limit case
- limit caps and offset-to-page conversion
- dry runs sending zero requests
- `confirm=True` sending exactly one POST with an Idempotency-Key, never retried
- path traversal and host override being rejected
- the repo allowlist
- https enforcement, with http allowed only for localhost and 127.0.0.1
- the token never appearing in results or caplog
- log redirects carrying no token, and hosts outside the list being refused
- retry bounds

**Unverified or worth knowing**
- **FMCSA:** I had no WebFetch tool, so these come from memory and are not checked:
  - the base URL `https://mobile.fmcsa.dot.gov/qc/services`, the endpoint paths, the paging parameters (start/size, assumed 1-based) and the WebKey format (only loosely validated)
  - the terms of use and the docs at https://mobile.fmcsa.dot.gov/QCDevsite/docs/qcApi
  - the README and module docstring say this.
- **GitHub log hosts:** the list of hosts that log downloads redirect to is unverified.
- **Idempotency-Key:** neither the Freight Recovery API nor GitHub documents honouring it (the platform source has no reference to it). It works as a correlation id only, which is why POSTs are never auto-retried.
- **Proxies:** `trust_env=False` means environment proxy settings are ignored. This is documented.
- **Paging:** `offset` must be a multiple of `limit`, because all three APIs page by page number.
- **Payload size:** with large pages (e.g. a claims pageSize of 100), the response can exceed 20 KB and comes back as truncated text.
